forms._readme: Client request on /work-with-us/contact/. 'client_request_endpoint': where the form POSTs (e.g. a Formspree URL); null = not connected: the page shows a 'Request by email' composer instead (same fields; its button opens the visitor's email app with a message to client_request_fallback_email), and npm run dev:notes adds a 'not connected' note. Set the endpoint and rebuild: the real form replaces the composer with no code changes. 'client_request_fallback_email': the shared club address only, never a personal one; it is the only email the build allows besides links.contact_email.

timeline._readme: Recruiting calendar on /join/ (stepper). Each step: name, optional (true shows an 'Optional' pill), description (null = no text), and optional dates. 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD) makes the step show its date and an 'Add to calendar' (.ics) download; add 'time' (24h 'HH:MM', local Eastern time), 'duration_minutes' and 'location' for a timed event. Unknown dates stay null: nothing is shown for them (no placeholder text). recruiting.current_step picks the highlighted step.

page_banners_readme: Banners behind the inner-page headers (components/page-banner.njk), keyed by URL. 'source': a bare file name looked up anywhere under assets/ (case-insensitive, any extension) or a path. If no file is found the page shows the plain maroon-black gradient banner, so dropping e.g. assets/photos/aboutimage.jpg in later is enough. 'band': which quarter of the photo's height to use (1 = top 0-25%, 2 = 25-50%, 3 = 50-75%, 4 = 75-100%); phones get the same band expanded to 16:9. 'focal': CSS object-position for the crop inside the banner. 'windows' (optional): exact [top%, bottom%] windows per breakpoint when a band would cut something off (see /team/). 'tint': maroon-black overlay opacity, 0.78-0.8 (0.78 keeps the gold eyebrow at 4.5:1 over a white sky). After a change: npm run build, then npm run banner-contrast.

/team/.windows_note: Band 3 (50-75%) cuts the back row's heads (hair starts at ~46%) and, as banners get narrower, the people at the left and right edges (faces span 7-93% of the width). Each window keeps band 3 as its centre (62.5%) and is just tall enough that every face stays visible at 1024-1440px (desktop), 768-1023px (tablet) and below 768px (mobile, whole photo).

/join/prepare/.note: Uses the /join/ banner exactly (same image, band, focal, tint and crop files). To give Prepare its own photo, replace this entry with { "source": "prepareimage", "band": 2, "focal": "50% 50%", "tint": 0.78 }.

/work-with-us/.windows_note: Band 3 (50-75%) cuts the walkers' heads (motion-blurred; the tallest reaches ~40.5% of the height, the rest ~46-50%). The window keeps band 3's centre (62.5%) and is widened just enough to 40-85% on desktop and tablet; phones get the whole photo (it is wider than 16:9).

/work-with-us/contact/.note: Uses the /work-with-us/ banner until a photo named contactimage (any extension) is added under assets/; then it is cropped at band 3 automatically.

work_with_us._readme: /work-with-us/ (Services). 'intro' and the 'engagement' items are the old Services page's own text (typos cleaned, nothing added). The two fee cards are read from faq.json ('How much do SCG services cost?'), one sentence each. 'help': the 'What we can help with' cards, derived only from projects.json skills; 'icon' is research, data, ai, process, marketing or business; 'link' opens /projects/ filtered (q = search, track = discipline); 'examples' picks up to 3 client logo chips from projects whose skills contain any of 'any' (or whose disciplines include 'track'). 'more' is the old page's closing line of 'How We Can Help'. 'engagement': the old page's five points; the first four are numbered steps, the fifth ('Beyond the semester') is the ongoing outcome. 'photo' is a file name in assets/photos (any extension), 'focal' (x% y%) is kept in the 4:3 desktop crop and 'focal_mobile' (optional) in the 16:10 phone crop made by npm run assets, 'badge' is the figure from the first point shown over the photo (decorative). 'frame_crop' (optional, e.g. '16:10') trims the first photo before it fills its desktop frame (here: drops the half-visible person at the left edge); without it the whole photo is used. 'photo2' is the second photo under the first (same fields; no badge). Desktop frames change shape with the text column, so each photo has 'focal_bands': [max frame aspect ratio (width/height; null = any wider), object-position], applied with container queries so that every face is either fully in or fully out of the frame; they were computed from the faces detected in the frame image (see DECISIONS). 'focal' is the fallback.

work_with_us.fee_cards_readme: The two cost cards above 'What we can help with'. Titles here; each description is one sentence of the FAQ answer 'How much do SCG services cost?' (faq.json). 'image' is a file name in assets/photos/ without extension (any of jpg/jpeg/png/webp); 'focal' (x% y%) is the point kept in the crop; 'alt' describes what the photo shows. npm run assets makes the crops.
